112:    matched edits nothing: do not open `docs/LEARNINGS.md` and do not add a

119: #### Gates — run these, do not skip them
120: 
121: These exist as scripts. Run them before committing; all three are non-destructive.
122: 
123: **A gate that asks about the FILE is not evidence about the PAGE.** §6 once rendered
124: every pane at once, with `tabset-accordion.js` throwing on every load, while the
125: sync gate, the copy translators, the asset gate and a tag-balance gate all passed.
126: The panes had stopped being direct children of `.tab-content`, so the CSS that
127: hides inactive panes stopped matching. The HTML still contained four panes, four
128: sets of check rows, and balanced tags.
129: 
130: `node tooling/render-check.js` is the check that sees this class of failure, and
131: **running it is part of claiming a layout change works** — not a nice-to-have.
132: `npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium` once.

140:    `<div class="score-highlight-body">`. Both are load-bearing: correcting either
141:    one alone breaks the layout, and removing the wrapper additionally collapses the
142:    check list into three columns. Verified by rendering every candidate. Leave
143:    them; they are not free-standing defects.

188: **CI is two workflows.** `.github/workflows/gates.yml` runs on push and PR: an
189: `offline` job that blocks (selftests, sync gate, skill mirrors, index freshness,
190: no hardcoded file key) and a `drift` job. `.github/workflows/figma-drift.yml`
191: holds the design-vs-code check and is triggered two ways — a **30-minute
192: schedule** and `workflow_call` from `gates.yml`. It is defined once and called,
193: because two copies of a drift report eventually disagree, and that report is the
194: thing you trust when it matters.
195: 
196: The drift check **never writes** — no `--apply`, no `--save`, no commit, no push —
197: and uses the existing read-only `FIGMA_API_KEY` secret. It needs no write access
198: to this repository. `gates.yml` does not block on it: it measures a canvas a
199: designer edits all day, and blocking a push because someone moved a frame would
200: be wrong.
201: 
202: **The loop, end to end.** Post a comment containing `@sync` on a section of the
203: CPP page; `sync-watch.js` resolves it to a component, translates any copy change
204: into the fragment and the page region, reports structural drift, runs the gate,
205: and — only with `--commit` — commits. A later push of `main` runs the gates.
206: The site publishes only when `main` is pushed.
207: 
208: **The two directions are separate, and only one of them is unattended.**
209: Figma → GitHub is automatic: the `sync-watch.js` daemon polls and applies. GitHub →
210: Figma is `figma-push.js`, and it is **report-only unless a human passes `--push`
211: and names the section.** Running both unattended on the same section would have
212: two agents overwriting each other, with the loser invisible. If you are unsure
213: which way a string should travel, leave it: the default writes nothing.
214: 
215: Everything is off by default: a bare run reports and changes nothing. It **never**
216: applies a removal, never creates or re-saves a baseline, never commits when
217: `sync-check` fails, and never pushes without `--push`. Processed comment ids are
218: remembered in `tooling/.sync-state.json` (gitignored) so nothing is done twice.
219: 
220: Use `--fixture <resolve-comment.json>` to drive the whole chain without posting
221: anything to the design file — testing this by leaving a live comment on the canvas
222: and waiting for a poll is a side effect, not a test.
223: 
224: **Component → Figma node is discovered, never declared.** `tooling/figma-discover.js`
225: walks the canvas and matches frame names to component directories: Figma names
226: frames with the pattern code (`HB05 - Large Desktop`, `AC01 - Desktop`,
227: `… — PN02`) and the code is the leading segment of the directory name
228: (`hb05-hero`). `tooling/component-registry.js` reads only that index.
229: 
230: There is **no `figma` block in any manifest** — it was removed from all 92. Two
231: hand-maintained sources (manifests and `ongoing_project/cpp/MAP.md`) disagreed, which is how
232: `hb05-hero` ended up pointing at a dead `43:*` node in a superseded file.
233: Discovery reproduces the hand-maintained `ongoing_project/cpp/MAP.md` mapping for 9 of 11 page
234: sections; the two it cannot are `site-header`, whose frames are named
235: `GN01`/`SN01` and have no derivable link to the directory name. Those are
236: reported unmatched rather than guessed.
237: 
238: Discovery skips the page named `Archives` (its frames are named exactly like the
239: live ones) and refuses hidden frames — this file parks `visible:false` drafts
240: inside the live page frame at the same y-range as the real sections. Both rules
241: are stated in the source. Ambiguous matches are ranked by a published rule and
242: every runner-up is printed.
243: 
244: To make a component comparable: give its frame a recognisable name, then create a
245: baseline deliberately. The tooling will not create one for you.
246: 
247: **The page is the reference; the first creation of a page is manual.**
248: `tooling/page-map.js` reads what each `index.html` is composed of and compares it
249: with the visible children of the page's Figma frame, so a designer adding,
250: removing or reordering a section produces a computable difference. The page's
251: frame is *derived* — take the components found in the page, look up their
252: discovered nodes, take the nearest common ancestor — so a second page needs no
253: configuration. Multiple pages are mapped independently.
254: 
255: Components are found in a page two ways, both deliberately strict: an HTML
256: comment naming `(components/<name>)`, and the component's whole fragment
257: occurring verbatim. Markers alone miss `site-header` (no marker) and §5 (legacy
258: marker string); content alone cannot be loosened — several components open with
259: identical `<div class="container fixed-grid">` boilerplate, and a short probe
260: matched four of them at the same offset.
261: 
262: **A pattern code is not a unique identifier.** `ac01-faqs` and `ac01-accordion`
263: both resolve to AC01. When one design frame is claimed by several components, the
264: **page decides** — it already states which variant it uses. A claim with no
265: claimant on the page is a *new* section whose variant is unchosen: it is reported
266: for a human rather than guessed, and it must not quietly drop out of the desired
267: structure.
268: 
269: **An ADD carries its CSS.** A section is a `<!-- <comp> fallback -->` anchor, a
270: `<style>` block holding `fallback.css` verbatim, a marker, and the fragment —
271: the arrangement `sync-check.js` asserts. Inserting the fragment alone would ship
272: unstyled and turn the gate red, so `--emit` produces all of it. A removal also
273: takes the component's `<style>` block, which sits *before* its marker and
274: therefore inside the previous section's region.
275: 
276: The emitted marker titles the section with the **component** name, not the Figma
277: frame name: a frame name is designer-owned and gets renamed, which would rewrite
278: the page on every design tidy-up.
279: 
280: `--add-items` on `figma-section-diff.js` is **not** a form of `--save`. It copies
281: only the positional `items` array into an existing baseline and rewrites no
282: oracle value, so the translator can pair items positionally against a baseline
283: written before `items` existed. It refuses if the copy has drifted. Use it to add
284: geometry; use `--save` only after the page has actually been updated.
285: 
286: Rules that follow from them:
287: 
288: - **Never re-save a baseline to silence a diff.** `--save` writes whatever Figma
289:   currently reports, with no check that the page matches. After a Direction-B
290:   write that makes the baseline *be* the code, and every later diff passes
291:   against a code-authored oracle. Known accepted divergences are recorded in the
292:   owning component's README instead.
293: - **Seed a baseline with `seed-baseline.js`, never with `--save`.** Seeding
294:   compares the design's copy against the shipped fragment first and refuses
295:   unless the page already carries every string the design has, so a baseline
296:   written that way records a design state code genuinely implements. After
297:   seeding, run `build-node-index.js` — the index discovers a baseline by its
298:   file existing, so it goes stale until regenerated.
299: - **§3 cannot be seeded mechanically.** Its hero frame holds a whole mock payment
300:   app inside its media slot (`supplier@sage-demo.com`, `invoice date`, a 🇺🇸 flag);
301:   only 26% of its 42 text items are page copy. `seed-baseline.js` reports it as
302:   `illustrative` rather than writing thirty meaningless strings into a baseline.
303:   A §3 baseline must be scoped by hand to the real copy.
304: - **Never let `translate-section.js` write without reading its report.** It is
305:   copy-only on purpose: it substitutes one string for another inside existing
306:   markup and refuses anything else, because an invented structure cannot be
307:   verified. It refuses a card **reorder** — the captions are the same set in a
308:   new order, so patching them would move each caption onto the wrong icon. A
309:   divergence declared in the component README outranks Figma; declare it in the
310:   ` ```divergences ` JSON block in that README, not in a sibling file.
311: - **Never auto-write `verify.json`.** `verify-section.js` asserts
312:   `got.includes(t.expectText)`; a tool that writes both the HTML and the
313:   expectation makes the assertion a tautology.
314: - **Never hand-edit `main.css`** (exported vendor bundle), and never touch a
315:   `SECTIONS` marker comment — the sync gate slices regions by those exact strings.
316: - **File keys: the live key is NOT written down here.** Read it with
317:   `python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('tooling/node-index.json'))['figma_file_key'])"`.

349:   - `/cpp` and `/cpp/` go nowhere on purpose: neither is redirected (no index

351:     signed-out one gets the wall like any other gated path.

354:   `team_YkHLrByo9aDI8NgtFeLmqet1`. No installed CLI on this box

391: 
392: - The Vercel CLI on this machine **has no persistent cached token** — the usual local

396:   (`NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` set to a corporate CA).
397:   Interactive `vercel login` is an HTTPS flow to `vercel.com` and can **hang** through
398:   that proxy. If a `vercel` command stalls, do not just retry it.

400: #### How to deploy when `.env.local` already holds `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`
401: 
402: A valid token may already exist locally in `.env.local` as `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`
403: (written by the Vercel CLI on a prior login). `.env.local` is gitignored
404: (`.gitignore` line `.env*`), so **never echo, print, or commit its value**.
405: 
406: The normal publish is a push of `main`, above. Use the CLI only when the user asked
407: for a production deploy and a `main` push is not possible. It spends the same Hobby
408: quota. Skip it while `api-deployments-free-per-day` is active.
409: 
410: When `.env.local` is present and contains `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, that fallback is:
411: 
412: ```sh
413: set -a && . ./.env.local && set +a && vercel deploy --prod --scope cwah123
414: ```
415: 
416: - `set -a && . ./.env.local && set +a` exports the variables from `.env.local` into the
417:   `vercel` process’s environment only — it does not print them.
418: - `--prod` targets the production alias. Drop `--prod` for a one-off preview deploy if
419:   you only need a review URL. A preview deploy spends the same daily quota.

422: 
423: - If `.env.local` is missing, or it exists but has no `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, the CLI will
424:   fall back to interactive auth and may hang via the corporate proxy. In that case:
425:   **stop and ask the user** for the deploy step they want to take, rather than retrying
426:   `vercel deploy` blindly.
427: - Never request OS-level elevation just to force a deploy through.

429: #### How to tell a deploy actually landed
430: 
431: - A deploy is not “done” when the CLI exits 0. Verify on the canonical URL:
432:   - The page serves the changed files (HTTP-check the changed asset URLs — e.g. a renamed
433:     icon should return 200, the old name should return 404).
434:   - The page’s `Last-Modified` / `X-Vercel-Cache` reflect a fresh build, not the prior
435:     cached deploy.
436: - For a production deploy, check `sage-prototypes.vercel.app`, not just a random
437:   deployment URL.

439: #### Independent live proof (no self-grading)
440: 
441: - The builder never declares its own work done. A "done / live / responsive"
442:   claim is proven only by a **separate auditor pass**: a fresh session with no
443:   build context, given the URL plus a pre-written bar (content strings, asset
444:   URLs, widths, interactions) — never by the builder's own screenshots.
445: - The auditor screenshots the asset **live on production** (viewing passcode
446:   in `docs/AUTH-SETUP.md`; `tooling/check-live-match.js --spec` automates the
447:   four proofs: content census, asset bytes, tap behavior, two widths) and
448:   reports measurements, not impressions. Byte-match of files is not proof;
449:   "appears on a small screen" is not responsive proof (two widths must render
450:   different layouts).
451: - **Audit criteria** (each reviewed against the product-UI doctrine —
452:   `skills/product-ui-curation/SKILL.md` and guidelines floor §4C — on
453:   2026-10-18; a bar that contradicts doctrine is itself a defect):
454:   1. **Content** — every source string present in the live DOM at the stated
455:      width (census, never eyeballed). A rung-removed element absent from the
456:      DOM is legitimate ONLY if its rung is declared and actually fires
457:      (dead-code rungs fail: doctrine "a rung that never fires is a claim
458:      about a picture that does not exist"). Missing string = FAIL.
459:   2. **Assets** — asserted ONLY for assets the live page actually requests,
460:      discovered from the live DOM (`<img src>`, CSS `url()`), never from a
461:      hand-written list (hand lists verify the wrong path — the 2026-10-18
462:      failure). Each discovered same-origin asset must byte-match its repo
463:      file. Unreferenced files are ignored, not asserted.
464:   3. **Behavior** — acts if and only if the design says it acts: real
465:      controls (tabs, accordion) must switch state live; picture-controls
466:      must be inert AND marked `role="img"`. Grading a picture as a broken
467:      form, or a dead control as working, both fail.
468:   4. **Responsive** — (a) no page horizontal scroll ABOVE the 360px UI
469:      floor; at or below it the sanctioned scroller must exist AND engage
470:      (guide floor doctrine — the blanket no-bleed bar was withdrawn for
471:      contradicting it); (b) ellipsis counts as clip (doctrine: "elision is
472:      a cut") — a clipped value means take another rung or grow the frame
473:      (min-block-size, never height), never silently pass; (c) NO mandatory
474:      layout difference — identical layouts across widths pass when nothing
475:      stops fitting; instead require rung-correctness: fired rungs declared
476:      with budget math, breakpoints at measured widths, no dead rungs.
477:   5. **One bar for every asset under audit.** The bar is written before the
478:      build and identical for all items — narrowing one item's criteria so
479:      the round "passes" is the same defect as self-grading.
480:   6. **Fidelity to the chosen source.** Live must match the approved source
481:      file at equal width (overlay + census — the verbatim-fragment
482:      doctrine). Deviations pass only as recorded exceptions, all three
483:      ways the doctrine demands: CSS comment with measured heights, README
484:      line, and the audit report. An audit that certifies a redesign
485:      against a responsiveness-only bar is void.

487:   what is still open (e.g. "Fortis: live HTML ✓ / AR: still PNG ✗"). A claim
488:   without its gap is a gloss, and gloss is the most expensive output there
489:   is — this rule exists because self-graded "done" cost a full session of
490:   rework on 2026-10-18. See `tooling/check-live-match.js` and the

494: 
495: - Do not put `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` or any other secret into a committed file.

499:   Vercel returns `api-deployments-free-per-day`, leave both alone: a refused attempt
500:   can slide the 24-hour window.
501: 7. Figma change to an existing page: if every section maps to a registered
502:    component, edit the HTML/TSX directly — no UI-kit round trip.

506: - MCP: `https://mcp.atomic-ui.sage.com/mcp/latest` (open, no OAuth). Offline
507:   fallback: `docs/atomic-ui-catalog.json`.

518:   `components/page-gate/` and, on Vercel, `middleware.js`. Sign-in and sign-up

## Figma read AND write (proven — do not claim otherwise)

Canvas write works from this repo via the remote Figma MCP server. Proven
twice against real files: `hello from Fledge Alpha` (2026-10-08,
`docs/FIGMA-MCP-WRITE-INSTRUCTIONS.md`) and `hello there from Muse` →
node `71:1040` in file `xZyOeTxZLVSiQY71qIHr6f` (2026-10-13, verified with
`get_design_context`).

- **Write tool:** `use_figma` on `https://mcp.figma.com/mcp` (remote server).
  Load official skill `.github/skills/figma-use/SKILL.md` before ANY
  `use_figma` call — its rules are hard requirements.
- **Connect skill:** `skills/figma-mcp-connect/` — open it when the Figma call fails to authenticate. It covers the
  OAuth-allowlist 403 and the stdio-proxy workaround this repo uses.
  Terminal shortcut needing no extra auth: `node tooling/figma-call.js
  <toolName> '<jsonArgs>'` (tokens live in
  `tooling/opencode-mcp-figma-remote/mcp-auth.json`, gitignored).
- **What CANNOT write:** Figma REST API has no node-mutation endpoint
  (`skills/figma-rest-api/` is comments/versions/dev-resources only);
  the desktop MCP server is read-only.
- **Fallback with no MCP:** plugin + local bridge
  (`tooling/figma-bridge/` + `tooling/figma-plugin/`, port 9876).
- Cross-file clone: no API for it — rebuild from library instances by key
  (`skills/figma-uikit-to-design`, `skills/pattern-page-to-figma`).
- **Edit + replace Figma componentry:** each Figma-editable component keeps
  `components/<name>/figma/spec.json` (paste source: keys, props, overrides)
  with `tooling/figma-export.js` (export), `figma-paste.js` (paste live
  instance), `figma-replace.js` (swap page instance, paste-then-delete).
  Workflow: `skills/figma-component-edit`. Pilot: `play-overlay`
  (round trip proven 2026-10-13 on scratch — paste, replace-keeps-position,
  cleanup).
- **Figma write rules of engagement** (`skills/figma-component-edit` §4,
  learnings 71–82): re-find nested nodes by name before every mutation and
  read back after (ids remap; silent partial applies are real);
  screenshots are truth, tree walks are not; resolve variables by KEY, never
  mirror live nodes; shared tree = rebase + gate + stage-own-files.

## The loop

**Search `skills/ROUTE.md` first.** One winner, in the order `skills/route/SKILL.md` states. Open only the file that row names. A task with no row is still this loop: add the row in the same commit. The table is this project's. The skill is the same process on any machine and in any project that copies `skills/route/`.

1. **Figma** design is the source. Open `skills/figma-mcp-connect` only when the Figma call fails to authenticate.
   Reviewer comments are triage input, NOT work orders: a stakeholder asking
   for grey-or-white (or black edges, or a component swap) gets a proposal
   and a user ruling on scope first — never a direct implementation. The
   2026-10-14 black-bar incident shipped unapproved canvas surgery through
   two systems (my hands, then the unattended sweep) and had to be reverted
   everywhere. No Figma or site writes from a comment until the user specs
   the treatment.
2. **Match each section to a component.** Registry first
   (`components/README.md`). If absent, the **pattern library is the source of
   truth** — harvest verbatim markup including its sub-elements (e.g. tertiary
   buttons REQUIRE `<span class="bottom-line">`; the bundle's `:after` green
   overlay only works with it). Use **Atomic UI only where the pattern library
   has no equivalent** (check via MCP + `docs/atomic-ui-catalog.json`).
   Copy markup verbatim — never hand-rewrite harvested layout/CSS
   (`skills/clone-web-element`).
3. **File the component** in `components/<name>/` with its README (`source:`,
   source URL, install snippet, used-in list) *before* composing the page.
4. **Build the page** under `prototypes/<slug>/` (or `ongoing_project/cpp/<slug>/`), including
   the Supabase comments block.
5. **Sitecore-bound work follows kit + pattern + variables — with a closest
   match, never a refusal.** Any page update an author must be able to remake
   in Sitecore may only use: UI-kit variant options (Layout page,
   `bxMYaGSeGh7inguTLvWp0I` node `278:64690`), pattern-demo markup verbatim,
   and kit variable values (`docs/kit-variables.md`, grep first). A requested
   value outside all three (e.g. padding 36) is NOT applied as custom CSS —
   instead propose the nearest PROVEN value with its numbers (36 → 24:
   |36−24|=12; 40 is arithmetically closer at |36−40|=4 but exists only as
   the large-breakpoint cell of `outer-padding-sm-small`, which has zero
   CMS-id saves — flag what proof it needs rather than offering it) and
   apply the chosen one through Figma + site + variables + instruction, or
   not at all. Making it possible and keeping it legal are the same job.
6. **Verify** in headless Chrome: full-page screenshots at 1440/1000/390px, zero
   failed requests, zero console errors.
7. **Commit + push `draft`.** That records the work and runs the gates. It does
   not publish the site. Publish only when the user asks: fast-forward `main` to
   that gated commit and push `main`. One push of `main` is one production deploy
   of `sage-prototypes.vercel.app` — `main` is Vercel's production branch and
   `vercel.json` enables deployments for `main` only. (The release branch was
   called `live` until 2026-10-16; no `live` branch exists.)
8. **Close on the route.** A run that followed a `node` command cell and
   matched edits nothing: do not open `docs/LEARNINGS.md` and do not add a
   heading there. Anything else edits `skills/ROUTE.md` in this commit,
   using the close in `skills/route/SKILL.md`. A When cell that already
   covers the task gets one trap sentence. A task the table has never seen
   gets one row. A script that draws the parts does not become a command
   cell. A trap is the refusal itself. It does not cite the learnings file.

#### Gates — run these, do not skip them

These exist as scripts. Run them before committing; all three are non-destructive.

**A gate that asks about the FILE is not evidence about the PAGE.** §6 once rendered
every pane at once, with `tabset-accordion.js` throwing on every load, while the
sync gate, the copy translators, the asset gate and a tag-balance gate all passed.
The panes had stopped being direct children of `.tab-content`, so the CSS that
hides inactive panes stopped matching. The HTML still contained four panes, four
sets of check rows, and balanced tags.

`node tooling/render-check.js` is the check that sees this class of failure, and
**running it is part of claiming a layout change works** — not a nice-to-have.
`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium` once.

Two rules learned the hard way about editing this markup:

1. **Render it. Do not reason about tag counts.** A depth walk says the document
   is fine; a browser says whether it is a tabset.
2. **Some deviations in these fragments cancel each other.** §6's Payments pane
   has an extra `<div class="score-style-box padding-none">` *and* an unclosed
   `<div class="score-highlight-body">`. Both are load-bearing: correcting either
   one alone breaks the layout, and removing the wrapper additionally collapses the
   check list into three columns. Verified by rendering every candidate. Leave
   them; they are not free-standing defects.

because two copies of a drift report eventually disagree, and that report is the
thing you trust when it matters.

Figma → GitHub is automatic: the `sync-watch.js` daemon polls and applies. GitHub →

and names the section.** Running both unattended on the same section would have
two agents overwriting each other, with the loser invisible. If you are unsure
which way a string should travel, leave it: the default writes nothing.

every runner-up is printed.

frame is *derived* — take the components found in the page, look up their
discovered nodes, take the nearest common ancestor — so a second page needs no

claimant on the page is a *new* section whose variant is unchosen: it is reported

therefore inside the previous section's region.

frame name: a frame name is designer-owned and gets renamed, which would rewrite

- The builder never declares its own work done. A "done / live / responsive"
  claim is proven only by a **separate auditor pass**: a fresh session with no
  build context, given the URL plus a pre-written bar (content strings, asset
  URLs, widths, interactions) — never by the builder's own screenshots.
- The auditor screenshots the asset **live on production** (viewing passcode
  in `docs/AUTH-SETUP.md`; `tooling/check-live-match.js --spec` automates the
  four proofs: content census, asset bytes, tap behavior, two widths) and
  reports measurements, not impressions. Byte-match of files is not proof;
  "appears on a small screen" is not responsive proof (two widths must render
  different layouts).
- **Audit criteria** (each reviewed against the product-UI doctrine —
  `skills/product-ui-curation/SKILL.md` and guidelines floor §4C — on
  2026-10-18; a bar that contradicts doctrine is itself a defect):
  1. **Content** — every source string present in the live DOM at the stated
     width (census, never eyeballed). A rung-removed element absent from the
     DOM is legitimate ONLY if its rung is declared and actually fires
     (dead-code rungs fail: doctrine "a rung that never fires is a claim
     about a picture that does not exist"). Missing string = FAIL.
  2. **Assets** — asserted ONLY for assets the live page actually requests,
     discovered from the live DOM (`<img src>`, CSS `url()`), never from a
     hand-written list (hand lists verify the wrong path — the 2026-10-18
     failure). Each discovered same-origin asset must byte-match its repo
     file. Unreferenced files are ignored, not asserted.
  3. **Behavior** — acts if and only if the design says it acts: real
     controls (tabs, accordion) must switch state live; picture-controls
     must be inert AND marked `role="img"`. Grading a picture as a broken
     form, or a dead control as working, both fail.
  4. **Responsive** — (a) no page horizontal scroll ABOVE the 360px UI
     floor; at or below it the sanctioned scroller must exist AND engage
     (guide floor doctrine — the blanket no-bleed bar was withdrawn for
     contradicting it); (b) ellipsis counts as clip (doctrine: "elision is
     a cut") — a clipped value means take another rung or grow the frame
     (min-block-size, never height), never silently pass; (c) NO mandatory
     layout difference — identical layouts across widths pass when nothing
     stops fitting; instead require rung-correctness: fired rungs declared
     with budget math, breakpoints at measured widths, no dead rungs.
  5. **One bar for every asset under audit.** The bar is written before the
     build and identical for all items — narrowing one item's criteria so
     the round "passes" is the same defect as self-grading.
  6. **Fidelity to the chosen source.** Live must match the approved source
     file at equal width (overlay + census — the verbatim-fragment
     doctrine). Deviations pass only as recorded exceptions, all three
     ways the doctrine demands: CSS comment with measured heights, README
     line, and the audit report. An audit that certifies a redesign

  what is still open (e.g. "Fortis: live HTML ✓ / AR: still PNG ✗"). A claim

  is — this rule exists because self-graded "done" cost a full session of
  rework on 2026-10-18. See `tooling/check-live-match.js` and the
  `live.spec.json` next to each verified component.

## Atomic UI rules (standard Sage UI)

- MCP: `https://mcp.atomic-ui.sage.com/mcp/latest` (open, no OAuth). Offline
  fallback: `docs/atomic-ui-catalog.json`.
- `list_components` → `component_details` → `list_examples` → implement.
  Never guess prop names; never hand-roll HTML/CSS that a component covers.
- Imports from `@sage/atomic-ui` only (icons: sanctioned family subpaths).
- Tokens via `theme.space` / `theme.colors` / `theme.radii`.
- Exactly one `AtomicProvider` at the app root.
- `src/patterns/*` are references, never imports.

## Hard rules

- **Every served page requires a signed-in @sage.com address.** The wall is
  `components/page-gate/` and, on Vercel, `middleware.js`. Sign-in and sign-up
  use the comment panel's email and password form (Sign in / Sign up, two
  buttons on one form).
  Forgot password returns to the same page. Any other address is refused, with
  a mailto to `chiwah.liu@sage.com` for an access request, and that contact
  stays on the form. After sign-in the browser stays on the URL that was
  requested — do not send people to `/` to sign in.
  Two bypass ids exist, both rows in `quick_signin_accounts` and both editable
  by the admin (panel → Reviewer tab → Access): a **viewing passcode** that
  opens pages in view mode only — commenting still needs a sign-in, and
  middleware re-resolves the pair on every document, so rotation kills stale
  cookies — and the **bot id** `bot` (`bot@sage.com`), which signs in as a real
  account and may comment.
  `node tooling/check-page-gate.js` fails if a full HTML page is missing the
  snippet. Do not add that snippet to a sync fragment (no `<body>`): the page
  region is compared byte for byte, and the gate sits outside it.
- **Comment identity comes from the token, never the form.** Posting requires a
  sign-in, and a DB trigger overwrites `author` from the JWT when signed in.
  Don't add a client-side trust path for `author` or `user_email`.
- **Secrets never enter the repo**: Figma tokens, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`,
  `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, Supabase `service_role`. Only the Supabase `anon` key ships to the frontend
  (RLS in `supabase/schema.sql` is what protects the table).
- **Never hand-edit `main.css`** — it is an exported vendor bundle.
- **No raw pixel/hex values** in new UI; use design tokens.
- **Custom CSS cites Atomic tokens.** Every hardcoded value in hand-authored
  CSS gets a row in `docs/TOKENS.md` (token name + provisional/verified).
  Snap new values to the Atomic `space` scale; flag near-misses instead of
  silently keeping them.
- A Figma frame cannot be cloned across files by MCP — rebuild from library
  instances by key (`skills/figma-uikit-to-design`).

## Shared skills (reusable from any project or device)

`skills/route/` is the process for choosing a job, including a job the
table has never seen. `skills/ROUTE.md` is this project's table. Copy the
skill and `tooling/check-route.js` into another project, start that
project's table from `skills/route/TEMPLATE.md`, and do not copy this
table with it. A commit carries the files. `git pull` on a laptop, a
desktop, or a VM is the install. Paths stay relative to the repo root.
